jev.routeExplained: When Skill suggestion is On, Jev may move a conversation that is still on Flint to Quartz, Coal, Blaze or Redstone for each new message. Off, the assistant you picked stays for every message. An assistant you chose yourself is never changed either way.
jev.activateExplained: Skills that are always-active, that match a trigger phrase, or that Jev picks are added to the prompt without you asking. Off, none is added for you; the model can still read a skill it sees in the catalogue, and you can still invoke one with /.
jev.modelRoutingExplained: For each new message in a chat or a Cowork session, Jev compares the model in use with the models you tick below and names another only when it is clearly better; most messages stay on the current model. Ask first: you are asked before a message goes to the other model. Always: it goes there without asking, and the reply names the model that answered. Your model picker is never changed, and a temporary chat is never sent to Jev. In Cowork only models that can use tools are offered, and none with a smaller known context window than the session's model. A hosted model sends that message to its provider.
jev.modelRoutingNeedsJev: Turn Skill suggestion On above, or Jev is not asked and the model you picked is always used.
jev.modelRoutingListHelp: Models Jev may choose from. A short note, such as "best for code" or "fast and cheap", helps it decide; it is sent to TypeSafe with the model's name and whether it runs here or is hosted. A model that cannot use tools is never offered in place of one that can, and only models that can see images are offered for a message with an image.
jev.modelRoutingNoModels: No usable models yet. Set up a provider with an API key, or install a local model.
jev.profilesToggle: Independent system prompt per type of work
jev.profilesExplained: Adds a short block to the system prompt for the kind of work each message asks for: review, planning, executing, refactoring, debugging, reverse engineering or explaining. Jev picks the profile from a session's first message when skill suggestions are On; otherwise a keyword match picks it. The profile stays for the session; change it from the picker in the Cowork header. Off, every run uses the global prompt alone. Edit each profile below.
jev.profilesAutoDesc: Picked from the session's first message: by Jev when skill suggestions are On, by keywords otherwise.
jev.title: Jev decision support (TypeSafe)
jev.pageDesc: Optional decision support from TypeSafe's Jev model. Off by default; Flint's own behaviour stays in charge.
jev.intro: Optional help from TypeSafe's Jev model ({{model}}, pinned). Both features are off by default and separate. Jev only suggests or reorders: Flint's permission checks, skill catalog, retrieved sources and agent behaviour stay in charge, and Jev never approves a tool. If Jev is slow, fails or is unsure, Flint does exactly what it does without it.
jev.keyConfigured: A key is stored in the protected secret store. It is never shown again or sent anywhere but TypeSafe.
jev.keyMissing: No key stored. Nothing is sent to TypeSafe without one.
jev.skillSends: Sends to TypeSafe, after you pause typing in Cowork: your message (first 2,000 characters) and the names and descriptions of this surface's skills. Suggests at most one skill as a chip you can use or ignore. Not sent for a message that already starts with /. Turning this on also sends your message the same way to pick an assistant and work style for it; that is skipped for temporary chats, short messages, and conversations where you chose the assistant yourself.
jev.rerankSends: Sends to TypeSafe, when a retrieval runs: the query (first 1,000 characters) and the text of up to 20 shortlisted passages (1,200 characters each). File names, paths and ids are not sent. Only the order changes; every citation keeps its source.
jev.modesExplained: Off: no request is made. Shadow: requests are made and decisions recorded below, but Flint behaves as if Jev were off — use it to compare before turning a feature on. On: the decision is used.
jev.noReceipts: No decisions recorded in this session.

coworkParallel.settingTitle: New sessions in a Git folder work in their own worktree
coworkParallel.settingDescription: Each new session attached to a Git repository gets its own worktree and branch (flint/<title>), so many sessions can work in one folder at once without touching each other or your checkout. Review, merge or discard each branch from the session.
coworkParallel.branchTitle: This session works on branch {{branch}}, in its own worktree
coworkParallel.mergeBody: Fast-forwards when it can and writes a merge commit when it must. If the branches conflict, nothing is changed and the conflicting files are listed.
coworkParallel.mergePending: The session's uncommitted changes will be committed to its branch first:
coworkParallel.alreadyMerged: {{base}} already has everything on this branch
coworkParallel.conflicts: Merging into {{base}} would conflict in {{files}}. Nothing was changed.
coworkParallel.discardLoses: This destroys work that exists nowhere else:
coworkParallel.discardNothing: Nothing in it is uncommitted or unmerged.
coworkParallel.notCarried: Not carried into the worktree: uncommitted changes in {{files}}.
coworkParallel.notCarriedCount: {{formattedCount}} uncommitted change(s) in your checkout were not carried over
coworkParallel.prPrompt: Commit any remaining changes, push branch {{branch}} and open a pull request into {{base}} that summarizes this session's changes.
coworkParallel.copyOffer: This folder is not a Git repository. Work on a copy so other sessions and your own edits are not touched; apply the changes back when ready.
coworkParallel.copyTitle: Changes go to a copy of {{folder}}; apply them back when ready

coworkParallel.binary: Binary or large file; no preview.
coworkParallel.deleteRemove: Remove its worktree and branch ({{name}}) too
